hindu_chitrangada.name: Trained as putrika-heir in warfare and the governance of Manipura
hindu_chitrangada.notes: Raised by Chitravahana as sole heir, schooled in arms and statecraft to continue the royal line; she fought alongside Arjuna.

hindu_dasharatha.name: Looses the sound-piercing arrow that strikes an unseen target by its sound alone
hindu_dasharatha.notes: His mastery of śabda-vedhī archery; on a hunt he kills the ascetic boy Shravana by this art, drawing the curse of bereavement that foretells his own death of grief.

hindu_dasharatha.name: Fights from a chariot in all ten directions at once
hindu_dasharatha.notes: The name Dasharatha, 'ten chariots', marks his command of a war-car that moves and fights in every direction; aided the devas against the asuras.

hindu_devaki.name: Bears Vishnu incarnate as her eighth child despite Kamsa's slaughter of her offspring
hindu_devaki.notes: Imprisoned with Vasudeva by her brother Kamsa, who slew her first children; her eighth son Krishna was borne to safety across the Yamuna.

sources.reference: Bhagavata Purana, Book 10; Vishnu Purana, Book 5

hindu_dhrishtadyumna.name: Springs full-grown and armoured from the sacrificial fire as the fated slayer of Drona
hindu_dhrishtadyumna.notes: Born of Drupada's vengeance-yajna performed by Yaja and Upayaja, fated from birth to kill Drona.

hindu_dhrishtadyumna.name: Marshals the Pandava host as supreme commander, arraying the daily battle-formations
hindu_dhrishtadyumna.notes: Commander-in-chief at Kurukshetra; deployed the krauncha, makara, shyena and ardhachandra vyuhas; beheaded Drona on the fifteenth day.

sources.reference: Mahabharata, Udyoga Parva and Drona Parva

hindu_drupada.name: Commissions the fire-sacrifice that yields children fated to destroy his enemies
hindu_drupada.notes: Humiliated by Drona, the Panchala king has Yaja and Upayaja perform a yajna producing Dhrishtadyumna (Drona's slayer) and Draupadi from the altar-fire.

hindu_indrajit.name: Wields the supreme missiles of the three gods — Brahmastra, Vaishnavastra and Pashupatastra
hindu_indrajit.notes: Taught the trideva weapons under Shukra; binds Rama and Lakshmana with the Brahmastra and felling-shafts.

hindu_kashyapa.name: Counts among the seven seers (Saptarshi) who order and people the cosmos
hindu_kashyapa.notes: One of the Saptarshi; husband of the thirteen Daksha-daughters, father of devas (by Aditi), asuras (by Diti), nagas (by Kadru), birds (by Vinata) and more.

sources.reference: Mahabharata, Adi Parva; Vishnu Purana, Book 1

hindu_kumbhakarna.name: Crushes armies with mountainous strength and devours hosts of warriors
hindu_kumbhakarna.notes: Roused from his half-year sleep, he wades through the vanara army; loses his arms to Rama's Vayavyastra and Aindrastra before being slain.

hindu_matsya.name: Founds the Matsya royal line and kingdom as the fish-born heir of Uparichara Vasu
hindu_matsya.notes: Boy-twin born of the apsara-fish Adrika; kept by Vasu as heir while his sister Satyavati went to the fishers.

hindu_dhrishtadyumna.name: Sword with which he beheads Drona

hindu_indrajit.name: Concealing celestial chariot won at the Nikumbhila rite

hindu_jatayu.name: Rending talons and beak that tear Ravana's chariot

hindu_kunti.name: Durvasa's mantra to summon any deity for offspring

hindu_dasharatha.gloss: Scion of the Raghu / Ikshvaku solar dynasty

hindu_draupadi.gloss: Daughter of (the sacrifice of) Yajnasena/Drupada, fire-born
The skilled chambermaid (her guise in Virata's court)

hindu_kashyapa.gloss: He of the unbroken wheel (a name of Kashyapa-Prajapati)

hindu_ganesha.name: Ganesha Chaturthi
hindu_ganesha.notes: Ten-day festival of Ganesha's birth: clay images are installed, worshipped with modaka offerings, then immersed (visarjana) on Anant Chaturdashi. Ganesha is invoked first in nearly every Hindu rite as Vighnaharta.

sources.reference: Ganapatya tradition; Mudgala and Ganesha Puranas

hindu_durga.name: Navaratri / Durga Puja
hindu_durga.notes: Nine nights culminating in Vijayadashami celebrate the slaying of Mahishasura; in Bengal the autumnal Durga Puja installs and immerses clay images. Recitation of the Devi Mahatmya (Durga Saptashati) is central.

hindu_kali.name: Kali Puja
hindu_kali.cadence: annual, new-moon night of Kartika (Diwali night in Bengal)
hindu_kali.notes: Worshipped especially at Dakshineswar and Kalighat with night-time rites; historically received blood (animal) sacrifice. Patron goddess of Bengal and of the Tantric tradition.

sources.reference: Shakta/Tantric tradition; Kalighat and Dakshineswar temple practice

hindu_krishna.name: Krishna Janmashtami
hindu_krishna.notes: Midnight birth of Krishna observed with fasting, vigils, jhanki tableaux and (in Maharashtra) the Dahi Handi; the great pilgrimage centres are Mathura-Vrindavan and Dwarka.

hindu_lakshmi.name: Lakshmi Puja (Diwali)
hindu_lakshmi.notes: On Diwali night homes are lit and cleaned to welcome Lakshmi for prosperity; the Sri Sukta is recited and Gaja-Lakshmi venerated.

hindu_hanuman.name: Hanuman Jayanti and Tuesday/Saturday worship
hindu_hanuman.cadence: annual (Chaitra Purnima) plus weekly on Tuesdays and Saturdays
hindu_hanuman.notes: Images anointed with sindur (vermilion) and oil; the Hanuman Chalisa is recited for strength and protection. As Sankatmochan he is invoked against adversity.

hindu_kartikeya.name: Skanda Shashti and Thaipusam
hindu_kartikeya.cadence: annual; Skanda Shashti (Aippasi) and Thaipusam (Thai full moon)
hindu_kartikeya.notes: Tamil Murugan worship centred on the six Arupadai Veedu shrines; Skanda Shashti reenacts the slaying of Surapadma (Soora Samharam), and Thaipusam features kavadi penance.

hindu_ganga.name: Ganga Dussehra and the Ganga Aarti
hindu_ganga.cadence: annual (Jyeshtha Shukla Dashami) and daily aarti
hindu_ganga.notes: Ganga Dussehra marks her descent to earth, observed with ritual bathing; the daily lamp-aarti at Varanasi, Haridwar and Rishikesh venerates her as the river of purification and moksha.

sources.reference: Mahabharata and Ramayana (Ganga's descent via Bhagiratha)

hindu_garuda.name: Garuda Panchami
hindu_garuda.notes: Celebrates Garuda's birth; venerated at the Garuda-stambha flagstaff before Vishnu shrines, embraced as an antidote to serpent-venom and Naga-dosha.

hindu_brahma.name: Pushkar Brahma worship at Kartik Purnima
hindu_brahma.notes: Pushkar holds the foremost (and rarest) temple to Brahma; pilgrims bathe in Pushkar Lake at the Kartik Purnima fair. Brahma otherwise receives little independent cult.

sources.reference: Padma Purana (Pushkara mahatmya); Brahma Temple, Pushkar

hindu_indra.name: Indra Dhvaja / Indrotsava (raising of Indra's banner)
hindu_indra.notes: A royal pole-banner of Indra was raised and worshipped for rain and victory; Indra is also the most-invoked deity of Vedic shrauta sacrifice (soma offerings).

hindu_kamadeva.name: Kama-Dahana at Holi / Vasanta
hindu_kamadeva.notes: Spring festival of love; effigies of Kama are burnt recalling Shiva's third-eye fire, and mango-blossom and sandal paste are offered to soothe him. Worshipped with Rati on Vasant Panchami.

hindu_bhishma.name: Bhishma Ashtami tarpana
hindu_bhishma.notes: On the day Bhishma quit his body, devotees offer water and sesame tarpana in his honour; the five-day Bhishma Panchaka vrata is observed in Vishnu temples. He revealed the Vishnu Sahasranama from the arrow-bed.

hindu_hidimba.name: Hadimba Devi worship at Dhungri, Manali
hindu_hidimba.cadence: continuous; Hadimba fair (May) and Kullu Dussehra
hindu_hidimba.notes: Deified as a kuladevi of the Kullu valley; her footprint on stone is worshipped at the Dhungri temple (1553 CE), and she leads the Kullu Dussehra procession.

sources.reference: Hidimba Devi (Dhungri) Temple, Manali; living Kullu cult

hindu_ghatotkacha.name: Ghatotkacha tree-shrine worship, Manali
hindu_ghatotkacha.notes: Worshipped at the deodar tree-temple near the Hidimba shrine in Manali, hung with iron weapons, horns, bells and red threads; one of the few places Ghatotkacha is venerated as a deity.

hindu_karna.name: Karna / Mahunag temple worship
hindu_karna.notes: Venerated as Daanveer in shrines across the north (Hastinapur, Karnaprayag, Deora) and identified with the deota Mahunag in Mandi, Himachal, where many shrines honour him.

sources.reference: Karna temples, Uttarakhand/UP; Mahunag (Karna) cult, Mandi, Himachal Pradesh

hindu_draupadi.name: Draupadi Amman firewalking cult
hindu_draupadi.notes: Worshipped as a Shakti goddess in Draupadi Amman temples across Tamil Nadu, with annual fire-walking (theemithi) festivals reenacting episodes of the Mahabharata.

sources.reference: Draupadi Amman cult, Tamil Nadu (theemithi/firewalking tradition)

hindu_jatayu.name: Jatayu veneration at Lepakshi
hindu_jatayu.notes: Lepakshi (Andhra Pradesh) is held to be where Jatayu fell; pilgrims honour the spot, Rama having performed the first funeral rites for the bird-king. A colossal Jatayu sculpture stands at Chadayamangalam, Kerala.

sources.reference: Veerabhadra Temple, Lepakshi; Jatayu Earth's Center, Kerala

attributes.name: Elephant head with a single broken tusk (Ekadanta)
attributes.notes: The broken tusk he used as a stylus to transcribe the Mahabharata; the elephant head signifies wisdom and the syllable Om.

Ten arms each bearing a different god's weapon
attributes.notes: Trishula from Shiva, chakra from Vishnu, vajra from Indra, bow from Vayu, conch from Varuna, and more, fused into one warrior body.

Lolling red tongue and dark (black/blue) body
attributes.notes: She stands on the supine Shiva, having halted her destroying dance on recognising him.

Yellow silk garment (pitambara), dark-blue complexion, flute at the lips in tribhanga stance

sources.reference: Puranic churning of the ocean; Indra iconography

sources.reference: Ganga iconographic tradition; Brahma Vaivarta Purana
